messages.subject: JSON data/sample format & Python interface
parts:
There's a boost lib that parses JSON into a
DOM-like property tree:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/doc/html/property_tree.html

We'd just need to implement our data interface on top of
a property tree the same way we have done for reading
from files and reading from the R environment.

I'm less clear on JSON output -- I don't see anything
to write JSON-formatted data, though it's bound to
be a lot easier than parsing if we need to write it
ourselves. The output needs to come in the form of
headers and then lines of data, and will hopefully be
streamable.

We might literally be able to set a compiled Stan
model up to work as a pipe taking JSON-formatted
data as standard input and producing JSON-formatted
data as standard output with control given by the
command-line options of the compiled Stan model. With
that, a fully-functional, basic Python interface should
be really simple.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] JSON data/sample format & Python interface
parts:
We don't actually need to get to or from R at any
point. RStan is a wrapper around Stan. We'd
write a PStan wrapper for Python and an MStan wrapper
for MATLAB, all of which would only depend on
Stan's code (which itself so far only depends on
Boost and Eigen libs).

I'd like to do one thing at a time, which in this
case, would be to write JSON input and output
parsers and generators for Stan. It'll be great it that'll make it
easier to run on clusters (or "in the cloud" as
the people with money like to hear).

We're only interested in integrating software without
copyleft encumbrances, so Avogadro is out. It's GPL-ed
from what I can see:

http://wiki.openchemistry.org/Avogadro

But all they seem to be using is jsoncpp. That site
looks like it's "public domain",

http://sourceforge.net/projects/jsoncpp/

which is usually what someone puts up who doesn't
understand licensing, see, e.g.,

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_domain_software

- Bob




On 3/3/13 3:32 PM, Tim Triche, Jr. wrote:
> Without reflection it seems like automated dumping of C++ objects is not possible, but if the data goes back to R in a
> standard form, this Kitware project seems to point the way:
>
> https://fosdem.org/2013/schedule/event/openchemistry/attachments/slides/175/export/events/attachments/openchemistry/slides/175/1230_Marcus.pdf
>
> While looking through their slides it dawned on me that, provided Stan can take input as JSON, that means that models
> can be stored in MongoDB and queued for testing. If Stan can output as JSON, that means the same is true of model/run
> output. And if both of those are true then you have a trivial cluster computing solution for running absurd numbers of
> models without a whole awful lot of setup or teardown.
>
> their implementation of IO with JSON/BSON (and HDF5, which is a smart idea):
> https://github.com/OpenChemistry/avogadrolibs/blob/master/avogadro/io/cjsonformat.cpp
>
> more: http://www.mail-archive.com/avogadr...@lists.sourceforge.net/msg00708.html
>
> A lot of the above just dawned on me, but regardless, Kitware is good people and they're probably right up the Taconic
> Parkway from Columbia ;-)

>
